item_title: AI-infrastructure stocks fell across the board Monday, the first real equity-market reaction to Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's weekend "pace the frontier" safety essay.
mechanism: Dario Amodei's "pace the frontier" essay was published as a safety proposal — coordinated, voluntary capability-slowdown, third-party evaluators — but equity markets re-priced it as a demand signal instead: if the labs actually slow the rate of capability gains, the hyperscaler capex line under the entire AI-infrastructure chain (chips, memory, EUV tools) has less growth to justify it, so the market marked down the whole supply chain simultaneously rather than any single company's own fundamentals changing. This is the same AI-equities/long-rates transmission mechanism capital-context.yaml's rate_regime reading flagged on 08-19 as showing up so far only through Japan's JGB leg (Nikkei/SoftBank/Kioxia/Arm falling together on a rates story) — today is that same "the whole chain reprices on one signal" pattern reappearing domestically, off a safety statement rather than a rate move.

scenarios.direction: The selloff is the first data point in a genuine capex-growth deceleration, not a one-day move, and hyperscalers actually trim guidance next earnings cycle.
scenarios.why: A same-day, sector-wide drop across chips, memory and EUV names — rather than one company missing its own numbers — is the shape a leading demand-growth signal would take, and it landed the same week Anthropic's own OpenAI counterpart used the identical framework to justify pulling its IPO timeline, i.e. a lab acting on the pacing logic with real capital consequences.
scenarios.precedent: The 08-19 JGB-driven Nikkei/SoftBank/Kioxia/Arm selloff read the same way in real time — rates repricing the AI-equity chain together — and proved transient within days, which argues against over-reading a single session but does not rule out this one being different.

scenarios.direction: This is a crowded-trade unwind, not a demand reassessment, and the sector recovers once positioning clears.
scenarios.why: 24/7 Wall St's own read of today's cross-section — Intel (least AI-exposed) falling hardest at ~7%, Nvidia (most AI-exposed) falling least at ~2-3% — is the opposite pattern from what a genuine AI-demand-growth scare would produce, where the most AI-exposed names should fall hardest.
scenarios.precedent: Nvidia's own OpenAI Ohio guarantee was cut from $250B to under $120B within three weeks (08-15) after investor pushback, then the broader AI trade absorbed that news and moved on within the same window — this map's own record that single risk-repricing events in this ecosystem have not so far compounded into sustained de-ratings.

context_note: No rating-agency or credit-market response has followed yet, so as of this window it is an equity-pricing event only, not (yet) a financing-cost event for the AI buildout capital-context.yaml's cross_border_credit and rate_regime readings track. Figures are premarket/early-session prices at write-up time, not confirmed closes.

item_title: The US 10-year Treasury yield closed in on 5% Monday, trading around 4.99% after touching 4.992% intraday Friday — its highest since October 2023 — as Friday's hotter-than-expected August CPI and oil-driven inflation pressure pushed September rate-hike odds to roughly 87-89%, up from 65-68% at the start of the month.
mechanism: Friday's hotter-than-expected August CPI (headline +0.4% m/m, core +0.3% m/m) landed the same week Saudi Arabia's pipeline shutdown and the Hormuz standoff pushed Brent above $108 — two inflation inputs, one data-driven and one supply-driven, arriving together and pushing September rate-hike odds from 65-68% at the start of the month to roughly 87-89% now. This lands directly on capital-context.yaml's rate_regime reading, which has been building toward exactly this test since the 08-24 TGA/buyback disclosure: Treasury's doubled long-end buyback ceiling (funded by a $935-950bn TGA balance, $350-400bn above the prior administration's target) was read at the time as "soft-form financial repression" escalating toward "fiscal dominance" — monetary policy subordinated to fiscal financing needs. A Fed that actually HIKES into that backdrop, rather than holding or cutting, is the scenario that would either confirm or break that framing, and Wednesday is the first real data point on which.

scenarios.direction: The Fed delivers a 25bp hike Wednesday and the long end does not retreat afterward.
scenarios.why: Would confirm the fiscal-dominance framing directly — Treasury's buyback/TGA mechanism continuing to absorb long-end supply while the Fed simultaneously tightens is the "coordinated or in tension" question capital-context.yaml posed after Warsh's 08-28 Jackson Hole speech avoided giving any reaction function at all.
scenarios.precedent: The 08-24 TGA-buyback disclosure itself: the 30-year touched a 19-year high of 5.33% intraday before pulling back only on the reporting of the mechanism, not on any policy easing — evidence the long end has already shown it can stay elevated through fiscal-side interventions alone.

scenarios.direction: The Fed holds instead, reading the oil/Iran-driven inflation component as supply-side noise rather than demand pressure, and the long end rallies on the surprise.
scenarios.why: Would be the first time this cycle a hawkish CPI/PPI run did not translate into hawkish Fed action — testing whether Warsh's committee actually treats a geopolitically-driven oil spike differently from domestically-driven inflation, a distinction his Jackson Hole speech never articulated either way.
scenarios.precedent: July's payrolls miss (-23,000 vs +83-85k consensus, published 08-07) was the sharpest data-side challenge yet to the hawkish bloc and still did not visibly soften the committee's public posture going into 09-16 — the precedent argues against a hold, but it is the closest comparable this map has.

context_note: capital-context.yaml's rate_regime reading (asof 2026-08-24) is now three weeks stale against this print — it captures the TGA/buyback mechanism and the Jackson Hole speech but predates both the CPI print driving today's yield move and the Hormuz/Saudi-pipeline oil spike compounding it. This entry is the update that reading needs at its next refresh.

item_title: August retail sales beat consensus hours before today's Fed decision,
mechanism: A hot consumption print landing the same morning as a near-certain hike removes the last plausible dovish surprise going into the decision, pushing the test of capital-context's "fiscal dominance" framing (can Treasury's TGA-funded buyback campaign hold the long end against a hiking Fed) from hypothetical to live today.

scenarios.direction: The Fed hikes 25bp with a hawkish dot plot and no pause signal.
scenarios.why: Today's data removes the dovish case; October/December hike odds are already priced at 39%/26%.
scenarios.precedent: The 2023 tightening cycle's pattern of consecutive hikes once a data-confirmed inflation resurgence broke a pause.

scenarios.direction: The Fed hikes but Chair Warsh's press conference signals a pause after, citing the bond market's own tightening (30-year near 5.2%, 10-year at 5%) as doing some of the Fed's work.
scenarios.why: Financial-conditions-already-tight arguments recur when long yields spike ahead of a decision.
scenarios.precedent: The Fed's 2023 "skip" logic after the regional-bank stress episode, cited explicitly for this kind of self-tightening argument.

context_note: Directly tests capital-context.yaml's rate_regime framing — a hike today, on top of Treasury's own yield-suppression buybacks, is the exact collision that reading has been building toward since the August TGA disclosure. The decision itself lands ~2pm ET, after this morning pass's window.

item_title: Brent eased on a reported inventory build even as the Saudi pipeline stays shut with no restart date,
mechanism: Two forces are pulling in opposite directions on the same barrel — a bearish inventory data point vs. a still-live supply disruption at a chokepoint capital-context's conflict_risk_premium reading already flagged as newly load-bearing (Saudi exports through Bab al-Mandeb running roughly 8x higher since Hormuz risk forced the reroute).

scenarios.direction: Oil resumes climbing if the pipeline restart keeps slipping without a date and Yemen fighting further threatens the Bab al-Mandeb corridor.
scenarios.why: This is now Saudi Arabia's primary alternate export route, not a secondary one.
scenarios.precedent: The 08-14 episode where Brent jumped 5%+ purely on "indefinite blockade" rhetoric with no physical incident — this market has already shown it will reprice hard on chokepoint risk alone.

scenarios.direction: Oil eases further if the inventory-build pattern continues and a restart date is actually named.
scenarios.why: Today's move already shows fundamentals-side data can outweigh unresolved-but-static supply risk on a given day.
scenarios.precedent: capital-context's own tracked pattern through mid-August of oil falling on OPEC/inventory data even as incidents accumulated.

context_note: Read against conflict_risk_premium's standing framing that Saudi's Bab al-Mandeb dependence turns the Yemen civil war (previously a separate thread from the Red Sea shipping story) into a direct oil-supply input.

item_title: Brent fell roughly 3.6% to about $102 Thursday as Saudi Arabia announced a concrete partial-restart plan for the East-West pipeline — half its 7 million bpd capacity back "within days," full capacity within about six weeks — while bypassing the damaged section, and separately began routing extra crude to Asian refiners via ship-to-ship transfers near Oman's Sohar port, just outside Hormuz.
mechanism: Two of this map's own standing risk premia are moving in opposite directions on the same event. Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline outage has been the load-bearing supply-side input behind Brent's run toward $108 since 09-10 — capital-context.yaml's conflict_risk_premium reading has tracked it explicitly as the mechanism turning Yemen's civil war into a direct oil-supply input, via the roughly 8x volume now rerouted through Bab al-Mandeb. A concrete restart timeline (rather than another undated "soon") removes that specific input at the exact moment rate_regime's own test — whether a hiking Fed needs oil-driven inflation risk to stay elevated to keep validating the "more hikes coming" dot-plot signal — is live. The two readings pull the same "is this inflation still supply-shock-driven" question in opposite directions on the same day.

scenarios.direction: The restart executes roughly on the stated timeline (half capacity within days, full within six weeks) and Brent continues easing from the $108 peak rather than re-spiking.
scenarios.why: Saudi Arabia restored this same pipeline to full capacity within days after an April 2026 attack — the precedent this outage has already exceeded once on timeline alone, but the mechanism (a fast, disclosed repair) is the same one now being invoked again with an actual number attached rather than "soon."
scenarios.precedent: The April 2026 East-West pipeline attack and its within-days restoration — this map's own thread record cites it directly as the comparison for how fast this specific pipeline can come back once Aramco discloses a plan.

scenarios.direction: The restart slips or the ship-to-ship workaround itself becomes a target, and Brent resumes climbing toward or past the $108 peak.
scenarios.why: The pipeline is Saudi Arabia's principal Hormuz-avoidance route; a workaround built specifically to dodge one chokepoint being forced to route through a second (Hormuz-adjacent Sohar transfers) concentrates rather than diversifies the war's remaining points of failure, and this war has repeatedly produced incidents this map didn't anticipate on stated timelines (the pipeline's own "soon" comment from 09-15 already slipped once before today's concrete plan).
scenarios.precedent: The 08-14 episode where Brent jumped 5%+ on "indefinite blockade" rhetoric alone, no physical incident required — this market has already shown it reprices hard and fast on chokepoint risk in either direction.

context_note: Read against conflict_risk_premium's standing framing that the Yemen civil war and the Red Sea/Hormuz shipping story are now mechanically linked through Saudi's own export routing, and against rate_regime's open question of whether Wednesday's hike needs continued oil-driven inflation pressure to stay validated by the data. A genuine pipeline fix, if it holds, removes one leg of the inflation case the Fed's own hawkish dot plot is resting on.

item_title: Late in this digest-day's own window — after the US close, and the day before its own reported due date — the Bank of Japan hiked its policy rate 25bp to 1.25%, the highest since 1995, on a split 7-2 vote, citing upside inflation risk.
mechanism: The BOJ hike is this map's cleanest test yet of the cross-border rate transmission channel capital-context.yaml's rate_regime reading has twice flagged as thin and The Cross-Border Rate Leg opened specifically to track: does a real, sized Japanese policy move (not just firming odds) now propagate into the same AI-financed, long-duration assets the US leg already prices off term premium? The JGB itself EASED on the hike (4.9bp lower to 2.947%) even as the policy rate rose 25bp — the hike was fully priced in, so the informative signal is not the JGB's direction but whether the weaker yen re-opens yen-funded carry trades into US/AI risk assets, or whether a hawkish, credible BOJ instead strengthens the yen's trajectory over the coming sessions and unwinds carry positions the way the 09-04 and 09-08 episodes on this map's own record already did twice this month on pure speculation alone.

scenarios.direction: The yen's initial weakening (to ¥156.64, continuing toward ¥157) holds or extends over the following sessions, carry trades stay funded, and Tokyo-listed AI proxies (SoftBank, Kioxia, Arm, Tokyo Electron) trade calmly rather than repricing.
scenarios.why: A split 7-2 vote with two reflationist dissents is a genuinely dovish-leaning hike relative to the near-unanimous hawkish consensus markets had priced (Reuters' poll put odds at 97%, OIS pricing as high as 97% too) — the size matched expectations exactly (25bp, not the larger move Takata had left open), which is the outcome least likely to force a rapid re-pricing.
scenarios.precedent: This map's own 09-01 entry: Japan's 10-year JGB first crossed 3% on pure speculation about a hike, and yields moved MORE on the anticipation than they have now on the actual, in-line decision — consistent with a "sell the rumor, hold the news" pattern rather than a fresh shock.

scenarios.direction: The yen's weakening reverses into renewed strengthening within days as markets read a hawkish BOJ (a hike delivered despite two dissents, "upside inflation risk" as the stated reason) as confirmation more hikes are coming, re-triggering a carry-trade unwind that drags Tokyo-listed AI proxies down together the way it did twice already this month.
scenarios.why: This exact mechanism has already fired twice on this map's own record in September alone — 09-04 (yen to a one-month high on hike speculation, Nikkei/SoftBank/Kioxia/Arm all affected) and 09-08 (yen to a seven-month high, Nikkei -1,130 points) — both driven by speculation ALONE, with no actual decision behind either move. An actual, delivered hike is strictly more evidence than speculation was, so the same mechanism firing a third time, on stronger evidence, is the live scenario this thread and The Cross-Border Rate Leg both exist to catch.
scenarios.precedent: The 09-08 entry on The Cross-Border Rate Leg: USD/JPY moved to 153.93 (a seven-month high) and the Nikkei fell 1,130 points (-1.70%) in one session purely on BOJ-hike bets, with the dollar index itself moving only a fraction as much — proof this specific FX pair moves the Tokyo AI trade on its own terms, independent of broader dollar strength or weakness.

context_note: Read against capital-context.yaml's rate_regime reading, which has twice deferred a "proper BOJ/JGB leg" as a /week-scale addition still not built, and against The Cross-Border Rate Leg's own watch line naming "09-18 is the first test" of whether the BOJ's hike PATH (not just probability) now sets terms independent of the US curve. This is that test's first real data point — size and vote composition, not yet the multi-session yen/Nikkei follow-through that would confirm either scenario.

item_title: CoreWeave's convertible-note raise grew rather than shrank between this morning's announcement and the close: upsized from $3.0bn to $3.7bn, priced at a 2.875% coupon due April 2033, with an initial purchasers' option for a further $500M within 13 days — and the stock sold off on the news rather than rallying, for a second time this thread has logged that reaction.
mechanism: CoreWeave's own backlog-vs-debt bet — the core question this map's CoreWeave Bet thread exists to track — just got materially more leveraged in one filing, and the market's reaction (a same-day sell-off rather than a rally) reads the raise as a credit-quality admission rather than confidence: capped-call transactions exist specifically to blunt dilution on conversion, which only matters if the market expects the notes to convert, which only happens if the stock performs — the instrument itself is a hedge against CoreWeave's own optimism about itself. This lands the same week this map's broader AI-buildout-debt-risk watch has tracked genuinely mixed signals on whether AI infrastructure debt is being priced as investment-grade-adjacent or as risk.

scenarios.direction: The sell-off is a one-day technical reaction to dilution mechanics and CRWV recovers within the week once the notes price and the capped-call structure is fully disclosed.
scenarios.why: Convertible-note announcements routinely produce a short-term "supply" overhang sell-off independent of the underlying business — this thread's own 09-11 entry already logged a comparable CoreWeave balance-sheet-driven drop reverse within a week on unrelated sector news (the Oracle backlog print).
scenarios.precedent: This thread's own 09-04→09-11 record: a "balance sheet concerns" 5% drop the same week Oracle's earnings beat pulled CoreWeave back up 4% in sympathy — the stock's balance-sheet-driven moves in this thread have not stuck without a fresh demand-side catalyst.

scenarios.direction: The sell-off holds or extends, becoming this map's clearest data point yet that credit markets are starting to price AI-neocloud debt as genuinely risky rather than a growth-story pass-through.
scenarios.why: This is the second instance logged on this specific thread of the market punishing rather than rewarding a CoreWeave financing move, and it arrives the same week Treasury yields are already elevated on the Fed's own hiking cycle — a worse macro backdrop for absorbing new corporate debt supply than earlier in the year.
scenarios.precedent: capital-context.yaml's rate_regime reading has tracked the 30-year Treasury auction clearing above 5% three times in 2026 as evidence the market is demanding real compensation for duration risk broadly, not just on sovereign paper — a backdrop this convertible offering is pricing into directly.

context_note: Directly on this thread's own watch line ("debt costs vs the AI-credit repricing") and adjacent to AI Debt Gets Rated's wider tracking of how AI infrastructure debt is priced across issuers — worth reading this raise's eventual coupon/conversion terms against that thread once pricing is confirmed.
